The golden arches glowed through the glass windows, casting a warm light on the plastic tables and red cushioned seats. The air carried a mix of fried potatoes, sizzling patties, and the faint sweetness of milkshakes.  

Two college students sat across from each other, trays pushed between them. One wore a slightly wrinkled hoodie with a university logo, earbuds hanging loose around his neck. The other, in a neatly buttoned shirt, tapped a pencil against a notebook resting on the table.  

“Man, this is way better than the hostel food,” the hoodie-wearer said, tearing open a packet of ketchup and squeezing it onto his fries.  

The other laughed, adjusting his glasses. “True. At least here the fries are *supposed* to be salty.”  

Their Big Macs sat half-unwrapped, steam curling out, while a pair of Coke cups sweated onto flimsy paper coasters. Around them, kids shouted from the play area, a cashier called out an order number, and the overhead speakers played a faint pop song.  

They ate in quick bites between bursts of conversation—talking about classes, exams, and the cricket match they planned to catch later. Despite the noise of the restaurant, there was a simple ease between them, the kind that comes from years of shared notes and late-night study sessions.
